content.content:
---
redu_schema: 2
repo: https://github.com/InvoiceShelf/InvoiceShelf
plan:
  tool: deploy_compose
  image: invoiceshelf/invoiceshelf:2.4.2
  port: 8090
  vm: m1.medium
  flavor_id: "3"
  database: managed postgres (redu-managed, own private VM, m1.small via db_flavor_id "2")
  hourly_cost_gbp: 0.0452
bootstrap:
  mcp: claude mcp add --transport http redu «REDACTED:env:78213b90» --client-id redu-mcp
  mcp_codex: codex mcp add redu --url «REDACTED:env:78213b90» --oauth-client-id redu-mcp
  source: invoiceshelf
quirks:
  - "⛔⛔⛔ WHO BECOMES THE ADMINISTRATOR: WHOEVER FINISHES THE INSTALL WIZARD, AND UNTIL THEY DO, ANY ANONYMOUS CALLER CAN LOG IN AS SUPER ADMIN WITH NO CREDENTIALS AT ALL. This is the single most important line in this file. routes/api.php:167-189 puts every /api/v1/installation/* route behind only the redirect-if-installed middleware, and RedirectIfInstalled.php:20-27 lets everything through until the profile_complete setting equals COMPLETED. One of those routes is POST /api/v1/installation/login, whose entire body (Installation/LoginController.php:20-21) is: take the first user whose role is super admin, and log them in. No password, no token, no check. Another, POST /api/v1/installation/database/config, runs migrate --seed --force, and the seeder (database/seeders/UsersTableSeeder.php:20-25) creates that super admin with an email AND a password that are both committed in the public repo. So from the moment the hostname resolves until the wizard is COMPLETED, the instance is there for the taking. FINISH THE WIZARD YOURSELF AS THE FIRST ACTION AFTER THE CONTAINER IS HEALTHY, BEFORE YOU HAND THE URL OVER, and then run the verification script in the body of this file to prove the window is shut. Never leave an unclaimed InvoiceShelf on a public hostname because it 'looks like a fresh install'."
  - "AFTER THE WIZARD, REGISTRATION IS CLOSED BY CONSTRUCTION, and that part is genuinely safe. There is NO public signup route anywhere in routes/api.php or routes/web.php: additional users are invited by an admin from inside the app. Anonymous requests can reach the login page, the forgot-password page, the per-company customer portal login at /{company}/customer/login, and the tokenised customer document links under /customer/invoices/{token} and friends, which are deliberately unauthenticated because they are what goes in an e-mail. Everything else, including every PDF route, requires an authenticated guard (app/Http/Middleware/PdfMiddleware.php:21). So the ONLY ownership problem is the wizard, and it is entirely a race against the clock."
  - "⛔⛔ SET APP_KEY EXPLICITLY, AND PASS THE SAME ONE ON EVERY REDEPLOY. Two separate failures if you do not. First: .env.example:3 ships a NON-EMPTY, COMMITTED APP_KEY, the entrypoint copies .env.example to .env when there is no .env (00-setup.sh:41-45), and the key:generate branch at 00-setup.sh:85-88 only fires when the .env has NO non-empty APP_KEY. It does, so no key is generated and the instance runs on a key that anyone can read out of the public repository. That key signs and encrypts every session cookie. Second: /var/www/html/.env is NOT on a mounted volume (only storage/ and Modules/ are), so the .env is rebuilt from scratch every time the container is recreated. Generate one yourself with `printf 'base64:%s' \"$(openssl rand -base64 32)\"`, pass it as the APP_KEY environment variable (inject.sh:15-17 writes it into the .env), and keep it with the deployment. Change it later and every session and every encrypted cookie stops decrypting."
  - "⛔ DATABASE: SET DB_CONNECTION=pgsql AND THE FOUR DB_* VARIABLES, OR IT SILENTLY USES SQLITE INSIDE THE CONTAINER. 00-setup.sh:47-60 treats an EMPTY DB_CONNECTION exactly like sqlite and copies a stub database to /var/www/html/storage/app/database.sqlite, and .env.example:10 is DB_CONNECTION=sqlite as well. It comes up perfectly healthy and every invoice, customer and payment lives in a file on the app VM. redu injects PGHOST, PGPORT, PGDATABASE, PGUSER and PGPASSWORD into the project .env and NEVER edits your compose, so map them yourself: DB_CONNECTION=pgsql, DB_HOST=${PGHOST}, DB_PORT=${PGPORT}, DB_DATABASE=${PGDATABASE}, DB_USERNAME=${PGUSER}, DB_PASSWORD=[REDACTED:value]}. Note the driver name InvoiceShelf wants is pgsql, not postgres."
  - "PROVE THE DATABASE WIRING TOOK, IN BOTH DIRECTIONS, BECAUSE AN ABSENCE ALONE IS NOT EVIDENCE. The image ships the postgresql-client binaries (docker/production/Dockerfile:10), so the positive half runs inside the container: `sudo docker exec <container> sh -c 'PGPASSWORD=\"$DB_PASSWORD\" psql -h \"$DB_HOST\" -U \"$DB_USERNAME\" -d \"$DB_DATABASE\" -c \"select count(*) from users\"'` must return a row count of at least 1 after the wizard. That is also what tells you your exec command worked at all. THEN the negative half: `sudo docker exec <container> ls -l /var/www/html/storage/app/` must show NO database.sqlite. If the first command errored, the second one's empty output means nothing. The VM runs docker, not podman, and the container is named after the compose project redu unpacks into, not after the service alone."
  - "⛔ LEAVE AUTORUN_LARAVEL_MIGRATION=false, AS UPSTREAM'S OWN COMPOSE DOES. It looks like the helpful thing to turn on and it BRICKS THE INSTALL. EnvironmentManager.php:90-94 refuses the wizard's database step with the error database_should_be_empty when a users table already exists, and the wizard is the only path to a completed install: there is no artisan command that creates the admin or sets profile_complete. Migrate at boot and you get an app that can never be installed. Leave AUTORUN_LARAVEL_OPTIMIZE=false too: the wizard REWRITES the .env at runtime (EnvironmentManager.php:47-81) and the controllers clear the config and route caches themselves around it (DatabaseConfigurationController.php:26-38)."
  - "⛔ DRIVE THE WIZARD THROUGH THE PUBLIC HOSTNAME, NEVER THROUGH LOCALHOST OR THE VM'S IP. EnvironmentManager.php:37-47 takes the HOST HEADER of the wizard request and writes it into SESSION_DOMAIN and SANCTUM_STATEFUL_DOMAINS. Complete the wizard against http://127.0.0.1:8090 on the VM because it is convenient and you have just pinned the session cookie to 127.0.0.1, which means nobody can stay logged in on the real URL, and the symptom is a login form that accepts the password and bounces straight back to itself. Use https://<the generated dname> for every wizard call."
  - "GENERATE THE DNAME YOURSELF, UP FRONT, IN FULL `invoiceshelf-<8 lowercase alnum>.redu.cloud` FORM, because three variables have to contain it at deploy time and a bare label gets a random suffix appended by redu that will not match. Set APP_URL=https://<dname> (with the scheme, it is validated as a url by DatabaseEnvironmentRequest), SESSION_DOMAIN=<dname> and SANCTUM_STATEFUL_DOMAINS=<dname>, both WITHOUT a scheme and WITHOUT a port: redu terminates TLS on 443, so the browser never sees 8090. Leave TRUSTED_PROXIES=\"*\" (TrustProxies.php:36 defaults to that anyway) or Laravel builds http:// URLs behind redu's proxy and the Sanctum stateful check fails."
  - "PORT: THE CONTAINER LISTENS ON 8080, THE COMPOSE PUBLISHES 8090, AND deploy_compose WANTS THE PUBLISHED ONE. Keep upstream's `8090:8080` mapping and pass port 8090. Health probe: GET /api/ping, which returns a small JSON object containing the string invoiceshelf-self-hosted (routes/api.php:129-133). Laravel's own /up is registered too (bootstrap/app.php:42). Use /api/ping rather than /, because / redirects to /installation until the wizard is finished and a redirect is a poor liveness signal."
  - "TWO VOLUMES, BOTH REQUIRED. /var/www/html/storage/ holds uploaded expense receipts, company logos, generated PDFs, the file-driver SESSIONS (SESSION_DRIVER=file) and the file cache; losing it logs everyone out and takes every uploaded document with it, while Postgres still lists them. /var/www/html/Modules/ holds any optional modules installed from the marketplace. Upstream mounts both and so should you. Note the storage mount is why 00-setup.sh:21-39 recreates the framework directories on every boot: a volume can arrive without them and Laravel then dies at boot with 'Please provide a valid cache path'."
  - "ONE DATABASE, SO THE MANAGED-POSTGRES TRAP DOES NOT APPLY HERE, and db_superuser is NOT needed. InvoiceShelf uses exactly one database and never issues CREATE DATABASE: the wizard connects to the database you name (EnvironmentManager.php:119-137) and runs migrations inside it. redu's managed Postgres serves exactly one database and refuses any other at authentication, which has broken other entries in this library; it cannot bite this one."
  - "RECURRING INVOICES WILL NOT FIRE ON THEIR OWN, AND THE DOCUMENTED WEBHOOK FOR IT IS DEAD ON 2.x. routes/console.php:16-30 schedules the invoice and estimate status checks and every ACTIVE recurring invoice through Laravel's scheduler, and nothing in this container runs `artisan schedule:run`: the image is nginx plus PHP-FPM. The intended hook is GET /api/cron with an x-authorization-token header, but CronJobMiddleware.php:18 compares that header with config('services.cron_job.auth_token') and config/services.php on the 2.x branch defines no cron_job key at all, so the value is null and the route answers 401 to everything. Say this plainly to the user rather than letting them find out when an invoice does not go out. The workaround is a crontab line on the VM running `sudo docker exec <container> php artisan schedule:run` every minute."
  - "PIN THE IMAGE, AND PIN IT ON THE 2.x LINE. Use invoiceshelf/invoiceshelf:2.4.2, which is the newest non-prerelease tag on Docker Hub (published 2026-07-29, the same day as the GitHub release). The repo's DEFAULT branch is 3.x and its README warns in its own blockquote that 3.x is an alpha preview and not for production data, so do NOT use :next, :3.0.0-alpha.2, :beta or :nightly. The image repo's README also says :nightly is transitional and will stop updating. Never write :latest into a recipe: it currently follows the v2 line, but the image README says it moves to a new major once that major is stable, and this application holds accounting records."
  - "NO migrate_command NEEDED, AND THAT IS NOT THE SAME AS 'IT MIGRATES ITSELF'. The wizard's database step runs the migrations (DatabaseConfigurationController.php:40). Nothing runs them at boot. That is the whole reason the wizard has to be completed as part of the deploy."
  - "THE IN-APP UPDATER IS DISABLED IN DOCKER, on purpose (there is a not-containerized middleware for exactly this). Upgrades are an image-tag change plus a redeploy with the SAME APP_KEY and the SAME managed database. Read the upstream upgrade guide before crossing a minor version, and take a database snapshot first: this is accounting data."
  - "NO SMTP ON A DEFAULT DEPLOY. Nothing is wired to a mail provider, so there is no password reset by e-mail, no invoice e-mailing and no customer portal invitations until MAIL_* is pointed at a provider the user owns. Say so at handover; until then the admin password is the only way in."
  - "SIZING IS AN ESTIMATE AND UPSTREAM PUBLISHES NO NUMBER. m1.medium (2 vCPU / 4 GB) is reasoning from what the image contains: nginx plus a PHP-FPM pool plus imagick and gd, with PDFs rendered in-process by dompdf, which is pure PHP and is the memory spike that matters. m1.small would probably serve a single user and would be the first thing to blame under PDF generation.
